item: A Stop is not an outcome of the host: the crawl rung no longer stamps an outlet it never visited, and the feed pass no longer stores the validator or climbs (or erases) the backoff for a feed the person's Stop cut short
refs: R327; R320; Export switch sweep D1 and D2; PR #1584
summary: Export's sweep drove every recorder with the production fetcher and the kill switch in each state a Stop leaves it in. D1: _lane_step_crawl stamped Source.last_crawled_at for outlets with 0 requests (switch engaged before the step) or 1 (cut in flight), sending them to the back of the rotation unvisited; the lane checks the switch only before it starts. D2: ingest_source stored the feed's ETag after a Stop mid-feed and climbed the backoff to 300 s, so the entries never asked for were not asked for again until the feed changed, and a Stop before the feed GET took the fetch-error branch that resets the backoff, erasing a quiet feed's history. The decision in code is kill_switch_active() read AFTER each step (R320), never the words of a refusal: the crawl step checks before each outlet, after discovery (no BFS fallback on a discovery the Stop cut short), after each sitemap page (the cut page is not counted as an attempt) and before the stamp; the feed pass checks before each entry and before the bookkeeping, leaving the row as it was so the next pass re-reads the feed with the old validator and dedup skips what is stored. A real host failure is still recorded (the controls). 12 tests use the sweep's harness shape (production make_fetcher, hosts *.example, a real request only with the switch engaged and cut by the airplane socket guard); each of seven statements, taken out, fails its own test. LIMITS: a Stop cleared again within one request's flight reads as the host's failure (the one-request window the law tracker states; the engagement-epoch mechanism that would close it is Export's proposal); the lane still starts later kinds after a Stop between steps (the lane-level pause is not part of this change); D3 (archive backfill) is Export's.
